metadata.title: A Ball at the Top Is Still Accelerating
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: At the very top of its flight, a ball thrown straight up has zero velocity. Is it still accelerating?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: Throw a ball straight up. As it climbs, its upward velocity shrinks steadily, until, at the very top of its path, the ball is momentarily at rest. At that instant, is the ball accelerating?
beats.new_visual_element: A red ball rises along a vertical dashed track; a teal velocity arrow v beside it starts long, pointing up, and shrinks as the ball decelerates, reaching a single dot exactly at the peak, where the ball freezes.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: dashed vertical track, ball frozen at the peak, velocity arrow reduced to a dot

beats.narration_text: At the peak, the velocity is exactly zero. The ball is not moving at that instant, so intuition suggests that nothing is happening to it, and that its acceleration must be zero as well.
beats.new_visual_element: Bold text ZERO VELOCITY stamps beside the frozen ball. Nothing else moves.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: frozen ball at peak, velocity dot, ZERO VELOCITY stamp

beats.narration_text: But acceleration does not measure velocity. It measures how quickly velocity changes. Ignoring air resistance, gravity changes the ball's velocity by nine point eight meters per second, downward, every second. At the peak, the velocity is passing from upward, through zero, to downward, without pausing.
beats.new_visual_element: The stamp fades. A thick black acceleration arrow labeled a = 9.8 m/s² appears beside the ball, pointing down. The ball begins to fall; the velocity dot regrows into a teal arrow pointing down, while the acceleration arrow keeps exactly the same length and direction.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: ball falling on the track, downward velocity arrow lengthening, fixed downward acceleration arrow

beats.narration_text: Compare three moments: rising, at the peak, and falling. The velocity points up, shrinks to nothing, then grows pointing down. The acceleration is identical at all three: the same length, the same direction, nine point eight meters per second squared, downward.
beats.new_visual_element: The single track transforms into three stacked snapshots (rising, at the peak, falling), each a ball with its velocity arrow and acceleration arrow. A gold box encloses the three identical acceleration arrows.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: three-row comparison: velocity arrows up / dot / down, acceleration arrows identical, gold box around the acceleration column

beats.narration_text: Zero velocity means only that the ball is momentarily at rest. Its acceleration was never zero. Gravity acts throughout the entire flight, including at the very top.
beats.new_visual_element: The snapshots transform back into the peak moment: ball frozen, velocity dot, black downward acceleration arrow. Text locks on: ZERO VELOCITY ≠ ZERO ACCELERATION.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: ball at peak, velocity dot, acceleration arrow, summary statement
